nodes.label: Coracao Presente Brand Mark
nodes.rationale: Square (approx. 512x512) raster logo for the 'Coracao Presente' gift shop. Full vertical lockup: a glossy red line-art emblem on top, the word 'coracao' set in a high-contrast didone-style lowercase serif beneath it, and 'presente' in a thin gold calligraphic script on the bottom line, flanked by small red hearts and hairline gold rules. Rendered on a soft cream/blush gradient ground with a warm light bloom in the upper right.

nodes.label: Heart-and-Gift-Box Emblem
nodes.rationale: A single continuous red ribbon-like line draws a heart outline whose lower half resolves into an open gift box with a bow, so one stroke reads as both symbols at once. Drawn as outline-only (no fill) with a gradient from deep crimson to bright red plus specular highlights, giving a glossy 3D ribbon feel. A tiny solid heart floats off the upper-right shoulder as a flourish. The merged heart/box is the literal picture of the brand name: a gift given with the heart.

nodes.label: 'coracao' Serif Wordmark
nodes.rationale: Set all-lowercase in a high-contrast didone/modern serif with the same red gradient and gloss as the emblem, tying the type to the mark. Lowercase keeps the tone warm and approachable rather than corporate; the Portuguese cedilla and tilde are preserved, anchoring the brand to a pt-BR audience.

nodes.label: 'presente' Gold Script Line
nodes.rationale: Second half of the name is deliberately contrasted against the first: thin gold calligraphic script instead of heavy red serif, creating a two-weight/two-color hierarchy so 'coracao' leads and 'presente' reads as a signature. Hairline gold rules and two small red hearts bracket the line, a common gifting/boutique convention.

nodes.label: Red, Gold and Blush Palette
nodes.rationale: Three-part palette: crimson-to-red gradient for the primary mark, muted metallic gold for the secondary script and rules, and a cream/blush gradient ground. Red carries the romantic/heart signal, gold signals premium gifting, and the blush ground keeps the composition soft rather than aggressive. This palette is the reusable source of truth for the storefront's accent colors.

nodes.label: Romantic Gifting Store Identity
nodes.rationale: Every element converges on one positioning: an affectionate, occasion-driven gift shop (Valentine's / anniversary / 'presente' gifting) rather than a general e-commerce catalog. Hearts, ribbon, bow, gold script and blush tones are all conventions of that category.

nodes.label: Square App Icon / Favicon Source Asset
nodes.rationale: The asset sits in public/ (served at site root) and is a 1:1 square raster, the shape web manifests and favicons require. Its role is therefore a static branding asset consumed by the PWA manifest / HTML head rather than an in-app content image.

nodes.label: Non-Transparent Baked-In Background
nodes.rationale: The cream/blush gradient appears painted into the raster rather than being transparent alpha. If so, the logo cannot be overlaid on dark or colored surfaces without showing a cream card behind it, and a separate transparent variant would be needed. Flagged as uncertain: alpha cannot be confirmed from visual inspection alone.

hyperedges.label: Vertical Logo Lockup Composition
hyperedges.rationale: Emblem, serif wordmark and gold script are stacked centered on one vertical axis in a fixed top-to-bottom order with descending visual weight. The three parts are only meaningful together as one lockup; splitting them into pairwise edges loses the stacking order and the shared centerline.

hyperedges.label: Dual Pictorial-Verbal Encoding of the Brand Name
hyperedges.rationale: The emblem encodes the exact same two words it sits above: the heart half is 'coracao', the gift-box-with-bow half is 'presente'. Picture and text say the same thing twice through different channels, so the mark stays legible with the type removed (favicon, app icon) and the type stays legible with the mark removed (plain-text contexts).

hyperedges.label: Warm Premium Surface Treatment
hyperedges.rationale: Gradient fills, specular gloss on the red ribbon, metallic gold script and a soft blush ground with a corner light bloom all belong to one rendering style. That style is what makes the asset raster-dependent rather than a flat vector, and it is why the background appears baked in.
